title: A webhook receiver
description:
Build the whole receiving side of webhooks: from raw HTTP bytes to the right handler, answering every delivery with the status that tells the sender the truth. It combines everything in this milestone.

```python
class WebhookReceiver:
    def __init__(self, secrets, clock, path="/webhooks", tolerance=300, memory=1000): ...
    def on(self, event_type, handler): ...
    def receive(self, raw): ...          # -> HTTP status
    ignored                              # ids of events nobody handles
```

`secrets` is a list of signing secrets (`bytes`, several during rotation); `clock()` gives the time in seconds. `on` registers the handler for an event type; a handler is called with the event dict.

**receive(raw)** goes through these steps and returns the status of the first that decides:

| Step | Status |
|---|---|
| Parse the request as in practice 4.04 (bodies up to 1 000 000 bytes); malformed | 400 |
| The path (without any `?query`) is not the receiver's path | 404 |
| The method is not `POST` | 405 |
| Verify the `Webhook-Signature` header against the raw body as in practice 4.02, with every secret, `clock()` as now and the tolerance; any failure | 401 |
| The body is not JSON for an object with a string `id`, a string `type`, a string `object_id` and an integer `version` (not a boolean) | 400 |
| The event `id` is remembered (a duplicate) | 200 |
| The object already has a version applied and this event's `version` is not greater (stale): remember the id | 200 |
| No handler is registered for the type: add the id to `ignored`, remember the id | 200 |
| The handler raises any exception: remember **nothing** | 500 |
| The handler returns: remember the id and the object's version | 200 |

Remembered event ids are bounded by `memory` as in practice 4.03 (the oldest are forgotten); object versions are always kept.
hints: Write the steps as a straight sequence of checks with early returns, in the order of the table. Reuse your parser from practice 4.04 and verifier from practice 4.02 as private helper functions.

Only the success path and the two "acknowledge and forget" paths (stale, no handler) remember the event id. The failure path must leave everything as it was, so the service's retry is processed normally.
requirements: Every delivery gets the documented status, decided in the documented order.
Only deliveries with a valid, recent signature from one of the secrets reach the event logic.
Each event is handled at most once, stale events never overwrite newer state, and events nobody handles are acknowledged.
A handler failure answers 500 and leaves the event retryable.
Memory for event ids is bounded.
unitTests:
import hashlib, hmac, json

SECRET = b"whsec_live"

class Clock:
    def __init__(self, t=1_000_000):
        self.t = t
    def __call__(self):
        return self.t

def delivery(event, t=1_000_000, secret=SECRET, path="/webhooks", method="POST", body=None, signature=None):
    raw_body = body if body is not None else json.dumps(event, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
    sig = signature if signature is not None else "t=%d,v1=%s" % (t, hmac.new(secret, f"{t}.".encode() + raw_body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest())
    head = f"{method} {path} HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: {len(raw_body)}\r\n"
    if sig:
        head += f"Webhook-Signature: {sig}\r\n"
    return (head + "\r\n").encode() + raw_body

def ev(id, type="order.updated", obj="o1", version=1, **extra):
    return {"id": id, "type": type, "object_id": obj, "version": version, **extra}

def make(**kwargs):
    clock = Clock()
    r = WebhookReceiver([SECRET], clock, **kwargs)
    state, calls = {}, []
    def update(event):
        calls.append(event["id"])
        state[event["object_id"]] = event["version"]
    r.on("order.updated", update)
    return r, clock, state, calls

@test("a delivery reaches its handler once")
def _():
    r, clock, state, calls = make()
    check_eq(r.receive(delivery(ev("e1"))), 200)
    check_eq(r.receive(delivery(ev("e1"))), 200)
    check_eq(calls, ["e1"])
    check_eq(state, {"o1": 1})

@test("HTTP problems")
def _():
    r, clock, state, calls = make()
    check_eq(r.receive(b"POST /webhooks HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n"), 400)
    check_eq(r.receive(delivery(ev("e1"), path="/other")), 404)
    check_eq(r.receive(delivery(ev("e1"), path="/webhooks?source=shop")), 200)
    check_eq(r.receive(delivery(ev("e2"), method="GET")), 405)
    check_eq(calls, ["e1"])

@test("signatures")
def _():
    r, clock, state, calls = make()
    check_eq(r.receive(delivery(ev("e1"), secret=b"forged")), 401)
    check_eq(r.receive(delivery(ev("e1"), signature="")), 401)
    check_eq(r.receive(delivery(ev("e1"), t=clock.t - 301)), 401)
    good = delivery(ev("e1"))
    tampered = good[:-2] + b"9}"
    check_eq(r.receive(tampered), 401)
    check_eq(calls, [])
    rotating = WebhookReceiver([b"new", SECRET], clock)
    rotating.on("order.updated", lambda e: None)
    check_eq(rotating.receive(good), 200)

@test("bad events")
def _():
    r, clock, state, calls = make()
    check_eq(r.receive(delivery(None, body=b"not json")), 400)
    check_eq(r.receive(delivery(None, body=b"[1]")), 400)
    check_eq(r.receive(delivery({"id": "e1", "type": "order.updated", "object_id": "o1"})), 400)
    check_eq(r.receive(delivery(ev("e1", version=True))), 400)
    check_eq(r.receive(delivery(ev(5))), 400)
    check_eq(calls, [])

@test("order and unknown types")
def _():
    r, clock, state, calls = make()
    r.receive(delivery(ev("e3", version=3)))
    check_eq(r.receive(delivery(ev("e2", version=2))), 200)
    check_eq(state, {"o1": 3})
    check_eq(r.receive(delivery(ev("p1", type="payment.created", obj="p"))), 200)
    check_eq(r.ignored, ["p1"])
    r.receive(delivery(ev("p1", type="payment.created", obj="p")))
    check_eq(r.ignored, ["p1"])
    check_eq(calls, ["e3"])

@test("a failing handler can be retried")
def _():
    clock = Clock()
    r = WebhookReceiver([SECRET], clock)
    attempts = []
    def flaky(event):
        attempts.append(event["id"])
        if len(attempts) == 1:
            raise ConnectionError("database down")
    r.on("order.updated", flaky)
    check_eq(r.receive(delivery(ev("e1"))), 500)
    check_eq(r.receive(delivery(ev("e1"))), 200)
    check_eq(r.receive(delivery(ev("e1"))), 200)
    check_eq(attempts, ["e1", "e1"])

@test("bounded memory")
def _():
    r, clock, state, calls = make(memory=2)
    for i in range(1, 4):
        r.receive(delivery(ev(f"e{i}", obj=f"o{i}")))
    r.receive(delivery(ev("e1", obj="o1", version=1)))
    check_eq(calls, ["e1", "e2", "e3"])
    r.receive(delivery(ev("e9", obj="o1", version=2)))
    check_eq(calls, ["e1", "e2", "e3", "e9"])
